paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of reasoning steps and the Pass@1 rate for two language models. The x-axis is labeled “Num. of Reasoning Steps” with a linear scale ranging from 5 to 40, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled “Pass@1 Rate (%)” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick labels at intervals of 20.  A blue line with circular markers represents GPT-4o, starting at the coordinate (5, 19.4) and increasing to (40, 83.9). The line shows a relatively steady increase between 5 and 10, reaching a value of 38.7 at x=10, then continues to rise to a value of 77.4 at x = 20. A light purple line with cross markers represents Claude-3.5-Sonnet, starting at the coordinate (5, 6.5) and increasing to (40, 89.2). This line increases from 6.5 at x=5 to 32.3 at x=10, then rises to 77.4 at x=20, and finally to 89.2 at x=40.
